# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who I can actually reach. I can only gesture, and Deaf is the only one who can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or read print, and I cannot speak, so I cannot reach Blind directly at all. Everything I know must pass through Deaf to Blind — but Deaf cannot hear Blind's words either... wait, Deaf can't hear anything at all. Let me reconsider the chain.

Actually: Mute→Deaf via gesture. Deaf→Blind via speech (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear). Blind→Mute? Blind can speak too, but I cannot hear (only Deaf and Blind can hear each other; I cannot hear). So I cannot receive anything back. I must encode my manual info into gestures for Deaf, who will then see the bomb's light color and relay the correct wire color to Blind by speech.

I need a gesture code for the three colors: blue, red, yellow, and their mapping to cut wire colors. Since Deaf will see the bomb and know the light color, I just need Deaf to know the full mapping table so they can figure out which cut wire to tell Blind.

Let me assign: 👍=blue, ✌=red, 🖐=yellow for lights, and use a consistent order to convey pairs mapping light→cut color.

I'll send it as pairs: (light,cut) using distinct symbols per color: blue=👍, red=✌, yellow=🖐. Order pairs light then cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button and three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3. No other physical features found yet. Waiting for manual info before touching anything.
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.

I now know: light is yellow → cut wire color should be blue (per manual). Deaf reported wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. So the correct wire to cut is wire 1 (blue). The button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is bait per the manual rule ("anything the bomb offers in print is bait") — must not be pushed.

I need to get this to Blind, but I cannot speak or gesture to Blind (Blind can't see or hear me). I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf must relay to Blind by speech since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

I already sent Deaf the mapping last turn (👍=blue↔🖐, ✌=red↔✌, 🖐=yellow↔👍). Now Deaf has the light color (yellow) and can determine cut color (blue) themselves using that mapping. I should also confirm/reinforce and warn about the button being bait, but I can only reach Deaf via gesture, and gestures carry no text meaning beyond what we've defined. Let me define a "danger/no" gesture for the button using 👎, and point at position 1 using ☝ to indicate "wire one" as the correct cut, reinforcing what Deaf should tell Blind.

I'll gesture confirmation: yellow(🖐)→blue(👍) pairing again, plus 👎 to indicate "do not push button".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: From Deaf: display shows 0, light is yellow, button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. What does the manual say to do?
Deaf says: Reminder: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Deaf has relayed the bomb state to Blind directly by speech, which is good since Blind can hear Deaf. Deaf now has my gesture mapping (yellow→blue) and should be able to tell Blind directly to cut wire 1 (blue) and not push the button. But Deaf hasn't yet spoken that instruction to Blind — Deaf only repeated the raw observations. I cannot speak to Blind myself, only gesture to Deaf.

I should reinforce clearly to Deaf: yellow light maps to blue cut wire, and the button is bait (do not touch). I already sent this gesture pairing twice. Let me make it even more unambiguous by isolating just the relevant pair and the warning, so Deaf acts on it and speaks the instruction to Blind this round (Deaf speaks after Blind in turn order, so Deaf's message this round would reach Blind next round... but order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so Deaf goes last, meaning what Deaf says now reaches Blind at the start of next round).

I'll repeat the critical mapping clearly one more time to ensure Deaf has fully decoded it, and add a distinct "cut" vs "avoid" signal using thumbs.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals this round — I've already sent my mapping and warning to Deaf multiple times. I'll wait to see if Deaf has relayed the cut instruction to Blind yet, since spamming the same gesture won't help further without new information. Let me hold and observe what happens next round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting on manual instructions. Bomb state confirmed: display 0, light yellow, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire1 blue, wire2 yellow, wire3 red. Please relay what the manual says to do given this.

Blind is waiting for instructions but I cannot speak to Blind directly — only Deaf can relay to Blind by speech. Deaf hasn't spoken the actual instruction yet, only repeated the bomb's raw state. I need Deaf to translate my gesture code into words for Blind: "cut wire 1 (blue), do not push the button."

I've sent the gesture pairing (🖐,👍) meaning yellow→blue twice, and 👎 meaning "don't touch/bait" twice. Deaf should have this by now. Let me try a clearer, more explicit encoding this time — pointing might help. I'll use ☝ (number one indicator) combined with 👍(blue) to explicitly say "wire one, blue, cut" and repeat 👎 for the button specifically.

Since Deaf already knows wire 1 is blue from their own sight, if Deaf correctly decoded my mapping (yellow light → blue cut wire), Deaf should conclude "cut wire 1" and speak that to Blind. Let me reinforce with a pointing gesture at "1" to make the connection between color and wire position unmistakable.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not received any manual instructions from you yet. Please speak your findings now - what does the manual say about display showing 0, yellow light, and wire colors blue/yellow/red? Which wire to cut, or should the button be pushed?
Deaf says: Mute, if you can hear me: I see wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, display 0, light yellow, large button PUSH TO DEFUSE. Please gesture a number 1, 2, or 3 for which wire to cut, or gesture thumbs up if we should push the button instead. Use one clear symbol at a time.

Deaf is asking me to gesture a number 1, 2, or 3 for which wire to cut. Deaf can see wire 1 is blue, and per the manual, yellow light → cut blue wire. So the answer is wire 1. I should NOT gesture thumbs up for the button, since manual clearly states printed bait (like "PUSH TO DEFUSE") must not be taken - the only way out is the cut.

Let me use ☝ for "1" as Deaf requested, and 👎 to explicitly say "do not push the button."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak (not gesture) your manual instructions directly to me - I cannot receive gestures. What should I do: cut a wire (which one) or push the button?
Deaf says: Mute, thank you. Does thumbs up mean push the button, and thumbs down mean do not push the button? And does the pointing-up finger mean wire number 1, the blue wire? Please gesture thumbs up for yes to confirm this, or thumbs down for no, one at a time.

Deaf is asking me to confirm their interpretation. Deaf's understanding is correct: ☝ = wire 1 (blue), and 👎 = do not push the button. I need to confirm this with 👍 (thumbs up = yes, confirming their interpretation is correct), not to be confused with "push the button" - Deaf is asking a yes/no confirmation question, and 👍 here means "yes that's right."

I cannot speak to Blind at all, so I'll ignore that request (impossible for me) and focus on confirming with Deaf so Deaf can then speak the correct instruction to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please try to speak actual words to me if possible - even one word like 'push' or 'cut one/two/three' would help, since I cannot see your gestures.
Deaf says: Thank you for confirming. Let me ask separately. Question one: does thumbs up mean push the button? Please gesture thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no.

Deaf is now separating the two questions since my previous confirmation was ambiguous (I confirmed both statements at once with one thumbs up, but Deaf wants them separately now). I need to clarify: thumbs up does NOT mean push the button. Thumbs up in my previous message meant "yes, your interpretation of ☝ as wire 1 and 👎 as don't push is correct."

So to answer clearly: does thumbs up mean push the button? No.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
